learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge of applied thermodynamics and heat transfer. Basic principles and their application to solving engineering problems.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, enabling them to learn new methods and theories, and providing them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Knowledge for carrying out measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert reports, studies, reports, work plans, and other similar tasks.
Ability to collect and interpret data and information on which to base conclusions, including, when necessary and relevant, reflection on social, scientific or ethical issues in their field of study.

Ability to identify their own training needs in their field of study and work or professional environment and to organize their own learning with a high degree of autonomy in all types of contexts (structured or unstructured).

Knowledge and understanding: Knowledge and understanding of the engineering disciplines specific to their specialty, at the necessary level to acquire the remaining competencies of the degree, including notions of the latest advances.

Engineering analysis: The ability to analyze complex products, processes, and systems in their field of study; choose and apply established analytical, calculation, and experimental methods appropriately and correctly interpret the results of such analyses.

Engineering projects: Ability to project, design, and develop complex products (parts, components, finished products, etc.), processes, and systems in their specialty, which meet established requirements, including awareness of social, health and safety, environmental, economic, and industrial aspects; as well as selecting and applying appropriate design methods.
Practical application of engineering: Understanding of applicable techniques and methods of analysis, design, and research and their limitations in their field of expertise.
Judgment making: Ability to manage complex technical or professional activities or projects in their specialty, taking responsibility for decision-making.
Communication and Teamwork: Ability to effectively communicate information, ideas, problems, and solutions in the field of engineering and with society in general.

Communication and Teamwork: Ability to function effectively in national and international contexts, individually and in teams, and to cooperate with engineers as well as people from other disciplines.

Distinguishes states of aggregation of pure substances and uses appropriate models to calculate their thermodynamic properties. Analyzes and discusses mass and energy balances of thermodynamic processes and cycles in closed systems.
Analyzes and discusses the performance, feasibility, and reversibility of thermodynamic processes and heat engines.
Makes decisions and evaluates the possible consequences of the selected alternative.
Defines the problem, the development of the solution, as well as the conclusions effectively, and making correct use of language, in writing.
Defines the problem, the development of the solution, as well as the conclusions effectively, and making correct use of language orally.
Analyzes and discusses mass and energy balances of thermodynamic processes and cycles in open systems, using the second principle of thermodynamics and the concept of entropy.
Coordinates work with other team members, contributes to the development of tasks and the creation of a good working environment within their team.

syllabus_topics: Basic concepts: Thermodynamic properties of fluids; Thermodynamic transformations; Thermodynamic state/transformation/cycle.
Properties: The state and phases of substances; Types of fluids; perfect, ideal, and real gases; P-v-T diagrams.
First law of thermodynamics: Transformations; Closed systems; Open systems or control volumes.
Second law of thermodynamics: Direction of spontaneous thermodynamic processes; Carnot engine; Efficiency of heat engines; Reversible and irreversible processes.
Heat engines: Internal combustion engines; Gas and vapor cycles; Refrigeration cycles and heat pumps.
teaching_methods: Project-based learning (PBL), including report writing and presentation

assessment_methods.method: Individual written and oral tests for the evaluation of technical competencies of the subject
Technical capacity, involvement in the project/PBL, work performed, results obtained, documentation submitted, technical presentation and defense

assessment_rules: Individual written and oral tests are evaluated for technical competencies. Resits for control points occur on the same day; if a score is below 5, a resit is mandatory, with the final grade calculated as 25% from the first attempt and 75% from the second. Project evaluations are continuous, based on team meetings and work progress. A final corrected report, addressing identified improvements, serves as the resit for project components.
